    2026 Masters Payout Highlights 
    • Winner: $4.5 million
    • Total Purse: $22.5 million
    • Runner-up: $2.43 million
    • Third place: Approximately $1.53 million 
    The Masters payout has grown significantly, increasing by $1.5 million from the 2025 purse. The winner also receives the iconic green jacket and exemption into all four majors for the following five years.

    What do caddies get paid at the Masters?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Caddies at the Masters can earn over $450,000 for a single win. They typically receive a weekly fee of $2,000–$4,000, plus a percentage of the player's winnings: 10% for a victory, 7% for a runner-up finish, and 5% for making the cut. For the 2026 purse, a winner's caddie takes home approximately $450,000 from the $4.5 million prize. 
    • Winner's Caddie Pay: ~10% of winnings (e.g., $450,000).
    • Runner-Up Caddie Pay: ~7% of winnings (e.g., ~$226,800).
    • Top-10 Finish: ~5%–7% of winnings.
    • Missed Cut: Caddies generally only receive their weekly base fee ($2,000–$4,000).
    • Expenses:
      Caddies are responsible for their own travel, lodging, and food, which is covered by the weekly wage.
    • Perks: Caddies at Augusta National have their own locker room and receive premium meals. 
    These payouts make the Masters one of the most lucrative weeks for caddies on the professional golf circuit.
